import os, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
def sh(*a, cwd=None, env=None):
    return subprocess.run(a, cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
c = tempfile.mkdtemp()
tar = subprocess.run(["git", "archive", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", c], input=tar, check=True)
env = dict(os.environ, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="t@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="t@example.com")
for cmd in (["init", "-q", "-b", "main"], ["add", "-A"], ["commit", "-q", "-m", "base", "--no-verify"]):
    sh("git", *cmd, cwd=c, env=env)
home = "/".join(("", "Users", "realperson", "docs"))
r = sh(sys.executable, "_tools/backlog.py", "new", "bug", "--commit", "--title", "planted leak", "--severity", "S3", "--repro", "python3 -c 'import sys; sys.exit(1)'", "--goal", "see " + home, cwd=c, env=env)
commits = int(sh("git", "rev-list", "--count", "HEAD", cwd=c).stdout.strip() or 0)
print("new --commit exit", r.returncode, "| commits after the base:", commits - 1)
shutil.rmtree(c, ignore_errors=True)
sys.exit(1 if commits > 1 else 0)

import os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
def sh(*a, cwd=None, env=None):

env = dict(os.environ, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="t@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="t@example.com")
for cmd in (["init", "-q", "-b", "main"], ["add", "-A"], ["commit", "-q", "-m", "base", "--no-verify"]):
    sh("git", *cmd, cwd=c, env=env)
count = lambda: int(sh("git", "rev-list", "--count", "HEAD", cwd=c).stdout.strip() or 0)
bl = lambda *a: sh(sys.executable, "_tools/backlog.py", *a, cwd=c, env=env)
home = "/".join(("", "Users", "realperson", "docs"))
repro = "python3 -c " + chr(34) + "import sys; sys.exit(1)" + chr(34)

r = bl("new", "bug", "--commit", "--title", "planted leak", "--severity", "S3", "--repro", repro, "--goal", "see " + home)
out = r.stdout + r.stderr
files = sh("git", "status", "--porcelain", cwd=c).stdout
problems = []
if r.returncode != 1:
    problems.append("new --commit exit %d, not 1" % r.returncode)
if count() != base:
    problems.append("new --commit made a commit")
if "leak-scan" not in out or "field goal" not in out:
    problems.append("the refusal names no leak-scan hit and field")
if home in out or "realperson" in out:
    problems.append("the refusal prints the value")
if ".json" not in files:
    problems.append("the item file is not left written and uncommitted: %r" % files)
shutil.rmtree(c, ignore_errors=True)
print("; ".join(problems) or "ok")
sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)

notes: Premise (planted clone, 2026-10-26): backlog.py new bug --commit --goal with a home-path shape built at run time exits 0, prints 'to fill in: field goal has a leak-scan hit' and commits it; backlog.py check refuses the same text afterwards, so the author rewords it in a second commit and the first stays in history, which kbgit.py publish refuses (BG-okrkeohe). Cause: bl_check.leak_errors runs only in backlog.py check; new, set and the other writers call commit_written without it. Fix in commit_written (_tools/bl_base.py), which every --commit goes through (referrers: bl_close, bl_items, bl_land, bl_plan, bl_upstream); mind the import direction (bl_base never imports bl_check; reuse bl_check.item_leak_hits and the clone allowlist as leak_errors reads them, do not copy the scan). No suite test: a bug gets its repro and user feedback (kb/_self/code.md); BG-okrkeohe's planted gate case covers the range. No claim on these files at planning. 2026-11-09 plan: set --commit already stops on the same hit (exit 2, file unchanged, via check) on this tree; only new --commit commits it. The fix keeps set as it is.
